sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.content: Nearly 45% of Indian organisations identify AI, digital, and data skills as their single largest workforce constraint [E1]. India aims to attract over $200 billion in artificial-intelligence infrastructure investment over the next two years [E2]. India's AI market is valued at approximately Rs 1.2-1.5 lakh crore in 2026 [E3].

sections.title: Market Insights
sections.content: Nearly 45% of Indian organisations identify AI, digital, and data skills as their single largest workforce constraint [E1]. There is an 82.9% GenAI skills gap in India [E4]. India could face a shortage of more than 1.4 million AI professionals by 2026 [E5]. India holds about 16% of the global AI talent pool [E6]. Only 25% of Indian organisations believe their workforce is adequately prepared to use AI effectively [E7].

sections.content: The accepted evidence does not identify enough verified companies providing products or services in the Artificial Intelligence market to support a company-level competitor comparison. sections.title: Evidence Requiring Review
sections.content:
These 8 statements could not be fully confirmed, so they are not used in the findings above. The reason for each is shown in brackets. Please check them before using them.
• The government has allocated ₹10,300 crore for the IndiaAI Mission over a five-year period [E8] (publication date unknown).
• A national GPU cluster is being established with 3,000 next-generation GPUs [E9] (publication date unknown).
• The India Semiconductor Mission has an outlay of ₹76,000 crore [E10] (publication date unknown).
• The India Semiconductor Mission has approved 10 semiconductor projects [E11] (publication date unknown).
• 39 per cent of current skill sets are expected to become outdated by 2030 [E12] (the wording goes beyond the quoted text).
• AI can deliver an additional 1.45 percentage points of annual GDP growth for India by 2047 [E13] (publication date unknown).
• Accenture projects that AI could raise India’s annual GDP growth rate by 1.3 percentage points by 2035 [E14] (publication date unknown).
• The ILO estimates that up to 70% of existing jobs in India are at high risk due to automation and AI [E15] (publication date unknown).

sections.title: Method and Limitations
sections.content:
AI-generated draft for consultant review. Not final client advice.
Numbers in square brackets, such as [E3], refer to the Evidence Appendix at the end of this report.
Facts checked: 58 accepted, 37 need review (the 8 most relevant are listed in the review section) and 12 rejected (duplicates, quotes not found on the page, or claims the quote does not support).
For 58 confirmed facts the final wording check could not be run, so their wording was not double-checked against the quoted text.
Estimates of the same market differ between sources. They are shown side by side, not averaged.
Dates come from page information and are approximate. Rules and schemes change, so check policy statements with the official source before relying on them.
